text: Welcome to my office. I see you are an adolescent experiencing delayed menarche and some unusual physical features; let's start by asking if you have ever had a broken bone or noticed any fractures with minimal trauma.

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient has not experienced menarche but was noted at birth to have ambiguous genitalia (partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly). Given her history of fractures, severe acne, and maternal hirsutism, do you have a family history of similar symptoms or known genetic disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (likely 21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth, primary amenorrhea, severe acne, and bone fractures strongly suggests chronic cortisol deficiency leading to increased sex steroids and impaired bone mineralization. I am requesting specific lab results to confirm. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, electrolytes, and bone density scan.
